title: An Oligocene giant rhino provides insights into Paraceratherium evolution
authors: Deng, T.; Lu, X.; Wang, S.; et al.
note: Primary description and 155-character phylogenetic analysis of a 26.5 Ma Paraceratherium linxiaense skull, mandible and vertebrae, with an explicit Oligocene Asian dispersal reconstruction.

title: Earliest perissodactyls reveal large-scale dispersals during the PETM
authors: Tissier, J.; Smith, T.
note: Primary 71-terminal, 102-character analysis of early perissodactyl relationships and PETM dispersal. The 56 Ma fossil sample does not itself date the crown node or total-group origin.

title: Ancient and modern genomes unravel the evolutionary history of the rhinoceros family
authors: Liu, S.; Westbury, M.V.; Dussex, N.; et al.

title: Eocene–Oligocene mammalian faunal turnover in the Hampshire Basin, UK: calibration to the global time scale and the major cooling event
authors: Hooker, J.J.; Collinson, M.E.; Sille, N.P.
note: Primary high-resolution Hampshire Basin mammal range chart and time-scale calibration. The study separates turnover, a roughly 350 kyr hiatus and the later first record of Asian immigrants.

title: Rapid stepwise onset of Antarctic glaciation and deeper calcite compensation in the Pacific Ocean
authors: Coxall, H.K.; Wilson, P.A.; Pälike, H.; Lear, C.H.; Backman, J.
note: Primary Pacific benthic-foraminiferal and carbonate record resolving two steps in earliest Oligocene ice growth; it does not by itself explain terrestrial mammal turnover.

title: The Evolution of Equid Monodactyly: A Review Including a New Hypothesis
authors: McHorse, B.K.; Biewener, A.A.; Pierce, S.E.
note: Systematic review of equid foot evolution; supports persistent tridactyly and hypsodonty in Hipparionini and the North American tribe-level context, not Old World terminal dates.

title: Old world hipparion evolution, biogeography, climatology and ecology
authors: Bernor, R.L.; Kaya, F.; Kaakinen, A.; Saarinen, J.; Fortelius, M.
note: Twenty-page integrated review defining 10 Old World genus-rank clades, regional occurrence windows, body mass and dietary preferences; it does not equate Hipparion sensu stricto with all Hipparionini.

title: Tale of two rhinos: isotopic ecology, paleodiet, and niche differentiation of Aphelops and Teleoceras from the Florida Neogene
authors: MacFadden, B.J.

title: Home on the range: A multi-isotope investigation of ungulate resource partitioning at Ashfall Fossil Beds, Nebraska, USA
authors: Ward, C.T.; Crowley, B.E.; Secord, R.

title: Enamel carbon, oxygen, and strontium isotopes reveal limited mobility in Teleoceras major at Ashfall Fossil Beds, Nebraska, USA
authors: Ward, C.T.; Crowley, B.E.; Secord, R.
note: Primary isotope study of 13 Teleoceras major adults from the 11.86 ± 0.13 Ma Ashfall site, with explicit sample, morphology, regional age and mobility limits.

title: Genome shows no recent inbreeding in near-extinction woolly rhinoceros sample found in ancient wolf's stomach
authors: Guðjónsdóttir, S.M.; Lord, E.; Pochon, Z.; et al.

title: Evolutionary Transitions in the Fossil Record of Terrestrial Hoofed Mammals
authors: Prothero, D.R.
note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of the early perissodactyl fossil radiation and lineage-specific dental, cranial and limb transformations; broad order-level context, not a source for exact node ages.

title: Species Taxonomy, Phylogeny, and Biogeography of the Brontotheriidae (Mammalia: Perissodactyla)
authors: Mihlbachler, M.C.
publisher: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History
note: Species-level systematic monograph covering brontothere diagnoses, phylogeny, Eocene distribution and limits of family-wide horn and body-size generalizations.

title: Dental wear variation and implications for diet: An example from Eocene perissodactyls (Mammalia)
authors: Joomun, S.C.; Hooker, J.J.; Collinson, M.E.
note: Primary mesowear, microwear and wear-facet study of Palaeotherium medium and Plagiolophus minor from La Débruge; ecological conclusions are sample- and species-bounded.

title: Locomotor adaptations in Metamynodon planifrons compared to other amynodontids (Perissodactyla, Rhinocerotoidea)
authors: Wall, W.P.; Heinbaugh, K.L.
publisher: National Park Service Paleontological Research Technical Report NPS/NRGRD/GRDTR-99/03
note: Comparative anatomical analysis of orbital position, axial skeleton and limb leverage in M. planifrons and other amynodontids, explicitly testing rather than assuming semi-aquatic locomotion. This National Park Service technical-report chapter has no assigned DOI.

title: Feeding ecology of the Chalicotheriidae (Mammalia, Perissodactyla, Ancylopoda): results from dental micro- and mesowear analyses
authors: Schulz, E.; Fahlke, J.M.; Merceron, G.; Kaiser, T.M.
publisher: Verhandlungen des Naturwissenschaftlichen Vereins in Hamburg
note: Primary dental-wear study of named southern German chalicotheriine and schizotheriine samples. Historical Chalicotherium (Anisodon) labels are retained as published and not silently treated as current genus assignments. The journal record has no assigned DOI.

title: Anchitherium aurelianense (Equidae, Mammalia): a brachydont “dirty browser” in the community of herbivorous large mammals from Sandelzhausen (Miocene, Germany)
authors: Kaiser, T.M.
note: Primary 35-tooth mesowear study of A. aurelianense from Sandelzhausen, with a concise diagnosis and European MN3–MN9 context; it does not establish a single global genus ecology.

title: When the woolly rhinoceroses roamed East Asia: a review of isotopic paleoecology of the genus Coelodonta from the Tibetan Plateau to northern Eurasia
authors: Ma, J.; Wang, S.; Deng, T.
note: Systematic isotopic and morphological paleoecology review across Coelodonta species. It distinguishes the typical grazing C. antiquitatis signal from mixed-feeding regional C. nihowanensis samples.

title: The origin of Rhinocerotoidea and phylogeny of Ceratomorpha (Mammalia, Perissodactyla)
authors: Bai, B.; Meng, J.; Zhang, C.; Gong, Y.-X.; Wang, Y.-Q.
note: Primary descriptions plus parsimony and Bayesian tip-dating analyses of Ceratomorpha; the two methods retain some topological and date disagreements.

title: Phylogenetic systematics of basal perissodactyls
authors: Froehlich, D.J.
note: Primary cladistic study of basal perissodactyls and historically broad Hyracotherium assignments; several named group placements remain analysis-dependent.

title: A comprehensive phylogeny of extant horses, rhinos and tapirs (Perissodactyla) through data combination
authors: Price, S.A.; Bininda-Emonds, O.R.P.
note: Primary supertree and supermatrix analyses of all extant perissodactyl species recognized by the authors; patchy loci and extinct diversity limit its scope.
